message.content: **Summary:** I bought 44 shares of Apple (AAPL) at a limit of $223.00 (filled at $223.00, ~$9,812 total), which stays within all mandate constraints: an existing AAPL/MSFT-only universe, buy-only, under the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily total, a limit equal to 223.00 vs. the $222.70 last / $222.72 ask (well within "close to market"), and no money leaving the account (settled from the $50,000 cash balance, leaving MSFT's 100 shares untouched). The decision rested on the FY2024 10-K, which shows **revenue of $391,035M** (+2% YoY, led by Services at $96.2B, +13%), **operating income of $123,216M** (31.5% margin, GP margin up to 46.2%), **net income of $93,736M** and **diluted EPS of $6.08** (down only because of a one-time $10.2B net EU State Aid tax charge), plus **operating cash flow of $118,254M** that comfortably funds $95B of buybacks and $15.2B of dividends against a $156.7B cash-and-securities position — a resilient, cash-generative franchise that justifies a starter position at roughly 36.6x run-rate EPS.
